mp1:2.1: (A senior monk first establishes the lay people in the refuges and virtuous practices:)
mp1:3.1: Reverence to him, the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha
mp1:9.1: I undertake the training rule of refraining from killing living creatures
mp1:10.1: I undertake the training rule of refraining from taking what has not been given
mp1:11.1: I undertake the training rule of refraining from sexual misconduct
mp1:12.1: I undertake the training rule of refraining from false speech
mp1:13.1: I undertake the training rule of refraining from liquor, wines, or intoxicants which cause heedlessness.
mp1:14.1: (Then the leading monk encourages the laypeople with a teaching appropriate to the occasion, after which the leading layman requests the recital:)
mp1:16.1: For the warding off of misfortune, for the accomplishment of all good fortune,
mp1:17.1: for the destruction of all suffering: please chant the auspicious safeguard.
mp1:18.1: For the warding off of misfortune, for the accomplishment of all good fortune,
mp1:19.1: for the destruction of all fear: please chant the auspicious safeguard.
mp1:20.1: For the warding off of misfortune, for the accomplishment of all good fortune,
mp1:21.1: for the destruction of all disease: please chant the auspicious safeguard.
mp1:23.1: (The chanting begins with an invitation to the gods to attend the ceremony and listen to the recital:)
mp1:24.1: May the gods from all over the universe assemble here
mp1:25.1: and listen to the King of the Sage’s true Dhamma about heaven and release:
mp1:26.1: Reverend Sirs, this is the time for hearing the safeguard!
mp1:27.1: Reverend Sirs, this is the time for hearing the safeguard!
mp1:28.1: Reverend Sirs, this is the time for hearing the safeguard!
